messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT - latency_regression detected for service=redwood-inference env=prod region=us-west p95=1.9s (SLO 1.2s) p99=6.8s (SLO 4s). Trigger: rolling-window spike. Paging oncall team.

anne: saw the page, I'm on it. kicking off quick triage — checking dashboards + recent deploys.

mike: oncall here. can you paste the grafana panel? I want raw query (no screenshot).

anne: Grafana link: https://grafana.redwood/d/latency/real-time?orgId=1&var-service=redwood-inference&from=now-15m

lucy: fyi there was a dedicated-runtime rollout 6m ago (canary to 10%). deploy-bot posted: 

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-15T18:05:23Z - rollout redwood-runtime:v2.3.1 -> canary 10% (author: kevin)

mike: ok suspicious. canary -> maybe kernel change or batching tweak. anne, can you run a quick compare of p95 across model routes?

anne: running quick prometheus queries: 
```
# p95 over last 5m by route
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
```
results: route="chat-stream" p95=2.6s, route="text-gen" p95=0.9s, route="embeddings" p95=0.2s

anne: streaming route looks hit the most. tail latency skewed.

kevin: I can pause the canary if we think it's the cause. lucy, any idea which commit might affect streaming tail?

lucy: commit c9f8a3 changed batching window heuristics and added an aggressive kv-cache eviction for long sessions. could cause cold-tail churn.

mike: good call. immediate mitigation options: 1) pause/rollback canary 2) pin routing to older runtime variant 3) increase autoscaler to absorb bursts 4) enable fallback model route for streaming. which do we want now?

anne: pause canary first. kevin, can you AP the runbook? (runbook link: https://runbook.redwood/pause-canary)

kevin: executing pause now. command: `scripts/deployctl pause-rollout --canary-id=2026-03-15-180523`

deploy-bot: Rollout pause requested by kevin. status: pausing -> in_progress.

sarah: Support here — any confirmed customer impact? I see a few user-facing errors in last 10m: increased 502s on streaming websocket sessions. Need an external comms draft if this persists.

anne: checking error logs from edge: lots of backend read timeouts during chunk fetch, correlates with active streaming sessions. Example trace id=tr_8b7f: 
```
[18:06:42] stream_chunk_fetch timeout after 4.0s (deadline)
[18:06:42] upstream: runtime-instance-12, kernel=fast-attn-v1
```

mike: that lines up with lucy's kv-cache change causing cache misses and extra DB reads. Before we escalate, confirm canary pause effect in 60-90s.

lucy: while pause in flight, we can also tighten prefix cache TTL to reduce churn: `configctl set runtime.kv_cache.prefix_ttl 30s` (current 5s). I can push for that if needed.

kevin: pause complete per deploy-bot: Rollout paused. canary traffic now routed back to stable.
deploy-bot: Rollout status: paused -> success.

anne: metrics update: p95 now 1.3s (improved), p99 4.5s (down from 6.8s). still above SLO but trending. streaming route p95 -> 1.7s.

mike: good. keep monitoring for 10m. lucy, hold on config change until we see stable for 5-10m unless more spikes.

lucy: ack. I'll prepare patch to kv-cache heuristics for review, but won't hotpatch unless needed.

sarah: I'll prepare a short customer-facing note (support triage): "We're investigating increased latency for streaming responses in us-west. We've paused a canary rollout and are monitoring. No data loss reported. We'll update within 30 minutes." anyone want to add?

anne: +1. add link to status page and mention model routes affected. status.redwood.com/incidents/3311114444

mike: postmortem owners: lucy (root cause), kevin (deploy/runbook), anne (metrics/monitoring), sarah (customer comms).

anne: quick operational notes to capture now: 
- action: paused canary (kevin)
- action: routing back to stable (deploy-bot)
- observation: streaming route worst hit
- immediate impact: transient 502s and elevated tail latency for ~10-20m
- next: monitor, consider kv-cache TTL tweak if spike returns

kevin: I'll run an infra health check on runtime instances (disk, network, qps). `infractl health --service=redwood-runtime --region=us-west`

mike: if p99 doesn't drop under 4s in next 10m, escalate paging to SRE mobile.

(5m passes)

anne: 5m update: p95=1.22s p99=3.9s streaming p95=1.25s p99=3.1s. errors have dropped to baseline.

mike: Looks stable. keeping watch. lucy, please proceed with a low-risk rollback of the batching tweak in the next maintenance window and open rollback PR.

lucy: will do. Opening PR now: https://git.redwood/runtime/compare/c9f8a3~1..c9f8a3 (rollback-batching-heurstic)

sarah: sending customer note now. draft posted to #customer-notices for review.

anne: closing the live paging thread in 30m unless there's a regression. Good job team. :thumbsup:

mike: agreed. post-incident: add a synthetic test for long-lived streaming sessions to catch kv-cache churn.

lucy: adding synthetic to our CI e2e suite and perf deck.

oncall-bot: Incident follow-up: create incident doc (template: https://templates.redwood/postmortem) and tag owners.

anne: will own the doc. assigning now.

sarah: thanks all, closing loop once postmortem published.

(END)
